The first evidence stream links Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside to Tyrosine--tRNA ligase, which is a known target of Cryptobeilic Acid B, and then to the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex. The second evidence stream provides a slightly weaker link, connecting Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside to Tyrosine--tRNA ligase via a different compound, [4-Hydroxy-2-(3-methylbut-2-enyl)phenyl] 2,4-dihydroxy-6-methylbenzoate, which also targets the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex. The combined evidence suggests that Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside may interact with the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex through a series of intermediate targets, though the strength of the evidence varies between the two pathways. The mechanisms involved appear to be consistent, with both pathways involving the Tyrosine--tRNA ligase protein as a central node. The evidence does not provide direct evidence of Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside interacting with the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex directly, but rather through its interaction with downstream targets.
